Understanding Gold & Silver
The foundational vocabulary: how to compare gold vs silver, what bullion forms exist, and what purity numbers actually mean.
Most first-time buyers walk into precious metals with two questions and a vague unease: should I buy gold or silver, and what am I actually supposed to buy once I pick one? The answers matter because the wrong product at the wrong premium can quietly cost you years of returns, and because gold and silver behave like genuinely different assets despite sharing a shelf at the dealer.
This path builds the vocabulary you need before you put real money down. By the end you will be able to compare gold and silver on the dimensions that actually drive decisions, recognize the major bullion formats sold in North America, and read a purity stamp without guessing. That foundation is what separates a deliberate buyer from one who pays retail markup on the first shiny thing a sales rep recommends.
📊
What you'll learn
How gold and silver differ as investments across volatility, liquidity, storage, and industrial demand
The main categories of gold bullion products and when each format makes sense
The main categories of silver bullion products and the premium tradeoffs between them
What purity numbers like .999, .9999, and 22k actually mean and why they matter for resale
